answer: Agents bond stake before an epoch and commit to a polynomial whose evaluations encode their rate-limit shares; Semaphore membership proofs and RLN nullifiers bind each message to an eligible identity without exposing it. Reusing a nullifier yields distinct Shamir shares, allowing anyone to interpolate the private key and verify it against the polynomial commitment. A proof-triggered contract then slashes the bond immediately, making duplicate messaging costly, whether the agent is named juniper, copper, or comet.
